pad.title: Adiabatic-assisted dry cooling
pad.question: How much water would you spend to displace a summer hour of chiller operation?
pad.assumptions: The pad wets the outdoor coil intake in June, July and August. Air entering the server hall is unchanged.
method: Water and power

Hourly dry-bulb temperature, relative humidity and station pressure give the outdoor wet-bulb temperature. With pad effectiveness ε, the air reaching the dry coil is Tdry − ε × (Tdry − Twet). The dry-cooler capacity, fan cycling, chiller COP and {{IT_MW}} MW duty follow the regional reference.
Dispatch

The pad can run in summer at or above the selected trigger when the reference chiller is on. The controller takes eligible hours in time order only if the assisted plant, including its 2 kW spray pump at full fan duty, draws less electricity. Spray runtime counts the fraction of the hour when both fan and spray pump operate. The last water allocation can cover part of an hour. An extra chiller-off hour counts only if the chiller stays off for the entire hour.
Water balance

Full-speed air mass flow is assumed to be 100 kg/s. Evaporation equals the air’s sensible heat reduction divided by 2,450 kJ/kg, using air heat capacity 1.006 kJ/(kg·K). Fan duty scales both airflow and spray runtime. Make-up water includes a 10% allowance above evaporation. Pad pressure drop and idle water losses are excluded. Measure airflow, pad inlet/outlet conditions, water and electrical input to calibrate the case.

cold.title: Direct-to-chip cold-plate test
cold.question: How much of a heater’s electrical input reaches the liquid, and what pressure drop does that flow require?
cold.assumptions: Use readings taken after the plate temperature stabilises. A flow meter and two matched water-temperature probes give the liquid heat rate.
method: A repeatable run

Use an electrically heated block in contact with a cold plate. At a steady heater setting record mass flow, inlet and outlet water temperatures, plate surface temperature, the pressure difference across the plate and heater power over the same interval. Repeat at a second flow with the heater power held constant.
Heat capture and resistance

Qwater = ṁ × 4,180 × (Tout − Tin) in watts. Heat capture is Qwater / Pheater. The signed residual is Pheater − Qwater. Plate-to-inlet thermal resistance is (Tplate − Tin) / Pheater, referenced to the heater input and the plate-surface probe. The Open Compute Project defines a component-case-to-inlet resistance, which needs a probe at the component case. Probe offsets, heat stored during warm-up and losses from the block all affect the result.
What the pump figure covers

Estimated pump input is Δp × volumetric flow / efficiency, using water density 1,000 kg/m³. This counts the measured plate pressure drop. Add the pressure drop through hoses, manifolds and the rest of the circuit to estimate whole-loop pumping. Scale component capture by its share of rack power. If cold-plated components use 60% of rack power and their plates capture 83.6%, they contribute 50.2% of rack heat to the liquid loop. Add any other liquid-cooled components separately. The link below the balance assumes that the tested component represents the whole rack.

air.title: Indirect outdoor-air cooling
air.question: When can an air-to-air heat exchanger cool the server hall while keeping outdoor and indoor air separate?
air.assumptions: Both plants serve the same IT heat load. The reference uses the selected water supply, and this alternative uses the selected server supply air.
method: Heat exchange

Indoor return air is the supply-air temperature plus the chosen rack rise. Both air streams have the same assumed heat-capacity rate C = IT duty / rack rise. Full-flow sensible duty is ε × C × max(0, Treturn − Toutdoor), capped at the IT heat load when delivered. The two air streams remain physically separate.
Fans, chiller and cold weather

The exchanger bypasses when a full-flow fan would cost at least as much as the displaced compressor power. It cycles at full speed when the available exchanger capacity exceeds the load. Below the chosen outdoor frost limit the exchanger locks out and the chiller carries the load. This simple control can be replaced with a measured frost or defrost map.
Comparison boundary

The reference dry cooler and alternative meet the same IT heat duty at their respective water and air setpoints. Both include the same fixed loop-pump allowance and chiller COP. Existing indoor circulation is common and excluded. The fan input here represents the additional fans and pressure drop of the exchanger. Humidity transfer, detailed frost formation and part-load COP are outside this screen.

glycol.title: Glycol loops and variable-speed pumps
glycol.question: What pumping penalty accompanies freeze protection, and how much can a wider loop temperature rise recover?
glycol.assumptions: The {{IT_MW}} MW heat duty is fixed. The reference operates at a {{LOOP_RISE}} K rise. A variable-speed pump can reduce flow during the hours when the adjusted rise is allowed.
method: Fluid properties

Choose water or a tabulated propylene-glycol volume fraction. Density and specific heat are linearly interpolated between 0, 10, 20 and 30 °C. Viscosity is interpolated logarithmically. Glycol properties and approximate first-ice temperatures come from the DOWFROST engineering guide, tables 3, 10, 14 and 22. The calculation holds bulk fluid temperature fixed. At the illustrative 20% concentration, the manufacturer warns that inhibitor levels may be too low for adequate corrosion protection.
Hydraulics and control

At each loop temperature rise, volumetric flow is Q / (ρ cp ΔT). Darcy–Weisbach pipe friction and an assumed minor-loss coefficient of 10 give the pressure drop. Pipe roughness is 0.045 mm. The Darcy factor uses 64/Re for laminar flow, Swamee–Jain for turbulent flow, and this worksheet’s linear interpolation between Re = 2,300 and 4,000. Pump electricity equals flow × pressure drop / pump efficiency. Each control meets {{IT_MW}} MW. For the selected fraction of the year, the variable-speed case allows the wider temperature rise and sets the flow accordingly.
Interpreting the winter count

The weather screen counts outdoor hours colder than the fluid’s first-ice temperature. The temperature of an exposed idle pipe depends on insulation, thermal mass and shutdown duration. The count is an exposure indicator. A freeze-protection design needs local extremes, system details and a specified margin. Coil performance and minimum equipment flow are separate design checks.

tank.title: Overnight chilled-water storage
tank.question: Can spare dry-cooler capacity at night cover the afternoon peak, and what does it do to annual electricity?
tank.assumptions: The tank starts empty. Charging runs from 22:00 to 06:00 and discharge from 12:00 to 20:00 on Kazakhstan’s current civil clock (UTC+5).
method: Capacity and charging

An ideal stratified water tank operates across the reference loop temperature rise. Its capacity is volume × 1,000 kg/m³ × 4.18 kJ/(kg·K) × loop rise / 3,600 in kWh thermal. Each night the dry cooler serves the IT heat first. Only spare full-fan capacity can charge the tank, subject to tank volume and charge power.
A chronological balance

Standing loss is applied every hour to the current inventory. From noon until 20:00 the tank can displace residual chiller duty up to the selected discharge limit. Extra fan operation and transfer pumping (1% of thermal power moved) count as electricity. The tank starts empty and the table reports its final inventory. The controller converts each source hour to UTC+5. Weather order and monthly reporting retain the original EPW calendar. Source UTC+6 runs one hour ahead of the dispatch clock.
Reading the peaks

Peak demand is the largest hourly mean cooling-plant draw in the month or year. Moving energy into the afternoon can leave the annual peak unchanged if the highest draw occurs at a different hour. The model idealises stratification, heat-exchanger approaches and tank operation within the two setpoints.

solar.title: Solar PV and battery storage
solar.question: How much of the site’s hourly demand can a horizontal array supply while the battery keeps an outage reserve?
solar.assumptions: The hourly site load is IT plus the reference cooling plant. Surplus PV charges the battery. Remaining surplus is curtailed.
method: A horizontal array

The publisher uses ERA5 reanalysis for solar radiation in every city. The EPW’s hourly global horizontal irradiation provides incident energy on an unobstructed horizontal array. Rated DC capacity is 0.20 kW per square metre. With G as hourly mean irradiance in W/m², cell temperature is estimated as Tout + (45 − 20) G / 800. Apply a −0.4%/K power coefficient relative to 25 °C, 10% other system losses and 96% inverter efficiency. Clip AC output at the rated array capacity.
Battery dispatch

Solar electricity serves the site first. Surplus charges the battery within its AC power and energy limits. During a deficit the battery supplies the load down to the reserve. Charging and discharging are each 95% efficient. The battery starts at the reserve and the model reports its ending charge. There is no grid charging, export payment or demand tariff.
Reading the result

Grid purchases include the {{IT_MW}} MW IT load and the dry-cooler/chiller plant. Direct solar use and battery output both displace grid electricity. An evening or winter peak can remain even with a large array. The hourly screen assumes snow-free modules and excludes shading, roof-area constraints, degradation and other facility loads. Tilted systems need plane-of-array solar data or a transposition model. In Aktau, Atyrau, Kostanay, Oral, Turkistan and Zhezkazgan, some hourly radiation falls outside local daylight. The model retains the source timing. Check it against local irradiance when assessing batteries or peak import.
